text:
mira: Heads up — since 02:00 UTC we've seen a cluster-wide uptick in NVIDIA Xid 13 and 31 on several p4d-like nodes in us-west-2. Symptoms: sudden CUDA driver resets, long tail latencies, and a handful of OOM-ish tracebacks.
jonas: saw this too, roughly same window. Do we have a quick correlation to model types or batch sizes?
anita: preliminary look shows majority of offending requests are from the realtime-llama-large fleet — batch_size spikes to 64 during morning jobs. Might be sustained seq_len=1024 workloads.
mira: attaching quick PromQL I used (copy/paste):
```
sum by(gpu_model, region, xid_code) (increase(node_gpu_xid_errors_total[1h]))
```
jonas: I ran that and got: p4d_v2/us-west-2 -> Xid13: 28, Xid31: 12, others ~0. Also p3dn has sporadic Xid48 but lower rate.
carlos: hardware note — Xid13 is typically illegal instruction or ECC/firmware triggered; Xid31 is GPU page fault/driver reset. Could be thermal or bad microcode. Any ECC counter bumps?
manually posted devops-bot: Automated alert: 28 Xid13s on nodename gpu-usw2-17 in last 60m. Ticket created: HW-4321.
anita: I pulled nvml/ECC metrics, ECC correctable errors count increased on gpu-usw2-17: 0 -> 14 in the window.
mira: sample nvml output from gpu-usw2-17 (trimmed):
```
GPU 0: Serial: 123ABC
ECC Errors: correctable=14, uncorrectable=0
Temperature: 78C
Power: 300W
```
jonas: temps are borderline but not catastrophic. However I also see repeated driver messages in dmesg: "NVRM: Xid (13): Parity/ECC error" and then "NVRM: Xid (31): GPU has fallen off the bus".
carlos: parity/ECC + fall off bus is suspicious for flaky PCIe lane or noisy power. Any recent BIOS/firmware pushes in that rack?
mira: we pushed a kernel/driver update two nights ago to the fleet for telemetry agent, but not GPU driver. No BIOS changes.
anita: workload angle: these trunks coincide with a change in model-serving config last week — increased max_batch_size to 64 for low-latency priority. Suggest we throttle that to 32 for the affected pool while we triage.
jonas: agree. I'll add a temporary routing policy to cap max_batch_size=32 and force small-batch lane for realtime-llama-large in us-west-2.
infra-oncall: action: marking nodes gpu-usw2-17,gpu-usw2-19,gpu-usw2-22 as scheduling:drain in the console. Notifying HW team.
carlos: I'll schedule a hands-on inspection tomorrow for the three serials. If ECC correctables continue to grow after drain+power-cycling, we'll RMA.
mira: we should also run a targeted repro: synthetic seq_len=1024, batch=64 traffic against a quarantined node to see if we can reproduce Xid. Anita, can you spin that up?
anita: yes, will deploy a canary job to the quarantined pool with telemetry. Test will run for 2 hours starting 03:30 UTC. I'll capture nvml counters + driver logs.
jonas: also enabling NVLINK and PCIe error counters in node exporter to get more granularity. PromQL to watch: `increase(node_gpu_pcie_uncorr_errors_total[5m])` and `increase(node_gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m])`.
mira: decision checklist: 1) throttle batch_size to 32 (done), 2) drain three suspect nodes (done), 3) run canary with telemetry (anita), 4) hw inspect + RMA if counters persist (carlos).
devops-bot: Note: rolling drain will reduce available capacity by ~6% in us-west-2. Autoscaler will try to spin up spare dedicated capacity.
anita: canary started at 03:30. Early signs: within 20m we reproduced 2 Xid13 on the quarantined node; ECC correctables ticking up.
carlos: that's sufficient evidence to RMA. Creating RMA request for serial 123ABC and two siblings. Hardware team will swap and reseat power cables this afternoon as interim step.
mira: follow-ups: - add a regression alert for sustained Xid13 > 5/hr per node - add a dashboard panel showing Xid by model route - add playbook entry: reduce batch_size/route to small-batch lane when Xid13 spike detected.
jonas: I'll open infra ticket INFRA-987 with the action items and link HW-4321.
anita: one more note — we should also examine model quantization/FP16 paths. Some kernels on FP16 mixed-precision trigger edge hardware states on older firmware. Adding a test for FP16-only workloads.
mira: thanks team. I'll post a short blameless summary to #incidents after RMA completes. :thumbsup:
jonas: ack, will follow up when RMA scheduled and nodes back in quota.
